_comment: Declarative deployment-dependency rules for deploy/ops/validate-deployment.py. Each rule says: WHEN a service declares a capability (a truthy flag / an env value / merely existing), it must REQUIRE the config that capability depends on — env vars, bind mounts, secrets, and config files. Adding a future check = adding a rule here (no code change). Categories covered: required-env, required-mount, feature-flag, secret, config-file. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md -> Deployment-dependency validation.

rules.why: RWE_FEED_POLL=1 starts the engine's in-process RSS poller, which resolves its feed list from RWE_RSS_FEEDS and reads the mounted feed file. Without both, rss_ingest.load_feeds() returns 0 feeds and the poller silently ingests nothing while appearing healthy (prod incident 2026-07-21).
rules.fix: On the `api` service add `RWE_RSS_FEEDS: /app/feeds/rss_feeds.txt` and the bind-mount `./rss_feeds.example.txt:/app/feeds/rss_feeds.txt:ro` — in the AWS override too, because its `volumes: !override` replaces the list.

rules.why: RWE_NEWSAPI_ENABLED=1 starts the NewsAPI adapter on the multi-source poller, which authenticates every request with RWE_NEWSAPI_API_KEY. Without the key the adapter stays disabled (a startup config warning fires) — the flag alone silently ingests nothing.
rules.fix: On the `api` service keep `RWE_NEWSAPI_API_KEY: ${RWE_NEWSAPI_API_KEY:-}` wired and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_NEWSAPI_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: Same chassis contract as newsapi-key: the enable flag without RWE_GUARDIAN_API_KEY leaves the Guardian adapter disabled (startup config warning) and silently ingests nothing.
rules.fix: Keep `RWE_GUARDIAN_API_KEY: ${RWE_GUARDIAN_API_KEY:-}` wired on the `api` service and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_GUARDIAN_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: Same chassis contract as newsapi-key: the enable flag without RWE_NEWSDATA_API_KEY leaves the NewsData adapter disabled (startup config warning) and silently ingests nothing.
rules.fix: Keep `RWE_NEWSDATA_API_KEY: ${RWE_NEWSDATA_API_KEY:-}` wired on the `api` service and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_NEWSDATA_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: Same chassis contract as newsapi-key: the enable flag without RWE_GNEWS_API_KEY leaves the GNews adapter disabled (startup config warning) and silently ingests nothing.
rules.fix: Keep `RWE_GNEWS_API_KEY: ${RWE_GNEWS_API_KEY:-}` wired on the `api` service and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_GNEWS_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: Same chassis contract as newsapi-key: the enable flag without RWE_MEDIASTACK_API_KEY leaves the MediaStack adapter disabled (startup config warning) and silently ingests nothing. (Free tier is ~500 requests/MONTH — keep the 5400 s interval + DAILY_BUDGET 15.)
rules.fix: Keep `RWE_MEDIASTACK_API_KEY: ${RWE_MEDIASTACK_API_KEY:-}` wired on the `api` service and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_MEDIASTACK_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: Same chassis contract as newsapi-key: the enable flag without RWE_CURRENTS_API_KEY leaves the Currents adapter disabled (startup config warning) and silently ingests nothing. (Google News RSS is keyless — RWE_GOOGLENEWS_ENABLED needs no companion rule.)
rules.fix: Keep `RWE_CURRENTS_API_KEY: ${RWE_CURRENTS_API_KEY:-}` wired on the `api` service and set the key in deploy/.env alongside RWE_CURRENTS_ENABLED=1.

rules.why: In production the engine fail-closes: it refuses per-user calls without RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET and refuses to boot if it is unset. It must be wired from deploy/.env (interpolated), never hardcoded into the compose file.
rules.fix: On the `api` service set `RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET:?set RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET in deploy/.env}`.

rules.why: The web tier signs engine calls with the same shared secret; it must be present, match the engine's, and be supplied from deploy/.env.
rules.fix: On the `web` service set `RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET:?...}` (identical to the engine).

rules.why: Google OAuth is the only production sign-in method; web/instrumentation.ts validates these at startup and process.exit(1)s if any is missing, so the web tier would crash-loop.
rules.fix: On the `web` service wire NEXTAUTH_URL + the three OAuth secrets from deploy/.env (`${NEXTAUTH_SECRET:?...}` etc.).

rules.why: Caddy is the only internet-facing process; it terminates TLS and reverse-proxies using the mounted Caddyfile. Without that config file mounted, the edge serves nothing.
rules.fix: On the `caddy` service keep the mount `./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro`.

rules.why: The engine's SQLite database and local backups live under /app/data; without the mount the DB would be created on the ephemeral container layer and lost on every recreation.
rules.fix: On the `api` service keep a volume mounted at /app/data (named volume in dev, host bind-mount in prod).

rules.why: GDELT is high-volume ingestion; catalog retention is OFF unless RWE_RETENTION_MAX_COUNT (or _MAX_AGE_DAYS) is set, so enabling GDELT without a bound lets feed_articles / the SQLite DB / every backup grow unbounded. (Guard checks the knob is WIRED; set a non-zero value in deploy/.env per the runbook.)
rules.fix: Wire RWE_RETENTION_MAX_COUNT into the api service and set a non-zero value in deploy/.env (e.g. 20000) whenever RWE_GDELT_ENABLED=1. See docs/GDELT_TRIAL_RUNBOOK.md.

rules.why: Identity recovery calls the engine from the auth path, and RWE_IDENTITY_RECOVERY is its documented rollback (set 0, restart web, no rebuild); RWE_BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS bounds that call. Both are read at call time, but `environment:` is an explicit allowlist and this stack has no `env_file:` — a variable absent from the service never reaches the container, whatever deploy/.env says. Both were absent when recovery shipped, so the rollback lever silently did nothing: an operator would set it, restart, see no change, and conclude the app was ignoring the flag.
rules.fix: On the `web` service add `RWE_IDENTITY_RECOVERY: ${RWE_IDENTITY_RECOVERY:-1}` and `RWE_BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS: ${RWE_BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS:-}` — in the AWS override too, since that is the manifest an operator reads during an incident. See docs/SESSION_IDENTITY_RECOVERY_DESIGN.md.

rules.why: Breaking-story detection runs on the engine's poller thread (story_events.detect_breaking_stories, hung off the same post-cycle seam as the story-cache warm) and is OFF unless RWE_BREAKING_NOTIFICATIONS is truthy. `environment:` is an explicit allowlist and this stack has no `env_file:`, so an unlisted flag can be neither turned on nor rolled back — setting it in deploy/.env would appear to do nothing, exactly the failure the web tier's identity-recovery lever hit. Unlike the API-key rules this one applies whether or not the flag is set: an OFF switch that cannot be reached is the problem it guards against. The two tuning knobs travel with it because they are what an operator reaches for when detection is too noisy or too quiet, at the moment they least want a redeploy.
rules.fix: On the `api` service (base compose, and restated in the AWS override) add `RWE_BREAKING_NOTIFICATIONS: ${RWE_BREAKING_NOTIFICATIONS:-0}`, `RWE_BREAKING_MIN_PUBLISHERS: ${RWE_BREAKING_MIN_PUBLISHERS:-}` and `RWE_BREAKING_TTL_HOURS: ${RWE_BREAKING_TTL_HOURS:-}`. Not on `ingest` — that service runs the one-shot rss_ingest.py, which never reaches the detection seam. See docs/NOTIFICATION_PLATFORM.md.
